task.name: An expiring escalate gate discards the advisory recommendation it just produced, so unattended runs fail stories the evidence had already resolved
task.story_text:
## Why

An escalate gate that expires discards the advice it just paid for.

On escalation the coordinator invokes a fresh-context advisor, which returns a report whose
`recommendation` is constrained to the action taxonomy and must appear among the options it
presents. That report is rendered for the operator, recorded on state, and then — if no
selection arrives before the gate expires — ignored. The run auto-escalates and the story is
recorded as failed, no matter what the advisor concluded.

The effect is that unattended operation has only two shapes, and neither is what an operator
actually wants overnight. Under `prompt`, every escalation becomes a failure after a fixed wait,
including ones where the evidence pointed clearly at a single action. Under `auto_approve`, the
gate short-circuits on gate-pass-plus-majority-approval and never consults the advisor at all, so
the cases the advisor exists for are exactly the cases it cannot help with.

What is missing is the middle: an expiry that applies the advice rather than discarding it. The
taxonomy already contains the answer for the case where no action is defensible — `elevate`
routes the story to a human design decision — so an advisor that cannot recommend confidently has
a way to say so, and an expiry that honours the recommendation inherits that safety rather than
being forced to guess.

The distinction this preserves is between a decision nobody made and a decision made on evidence.
An operator returning in the morning needs to know which one they are looking at, for each story
and without reconstructing the run.

## Example

A story escalates at 02:00 with the gate passing and one unresolved P2, and the advisor
recommends `land_core_defer_edges` with its reasoning recorded.

Today, at 02:10 the run logs `Pending decision timed out after 10m 0s — auto-escalating`, the
story is recorded as failed, and the recommendation is preserved only as an artifact nobody acted
on. The operator arrives to a failed story, reads the advice, agrees with it, and performs by hand
the action the system had already selected eight hours earlier.

Wanted: at 02:10 the run records that the gate expired and the advisor's recommendation was
applied, lands the core, files the deferred edge, and the morning view shows the story as landed
by advice rather than by an operator — with the same reasoning attached. Had the advisor instead
returned `elevate`, or returned nothing at all, the story would be waiting exactly as it does
today.

## Acceptance criteria

- An escalate gate that expires without an operator selection applies the advisory
  recommendation, and the outcome is the same as if an operator had chosen that action
  deliberately.
- A recommendation of `elevate` on expiry leaves the story awaiting a human, because the taxonomy
  already treats it as the answer for a case no automated choice fits.
- When no recommendation is available to apply — the advisor failed to launch, produced no
  parseable report, or recommended nothing — the gate preserves the story for an operator rather
  than selecting a fallback action. An absent recommendation is the absence of advice, not
  consent to any particular outcome, and the run states which of those two situations occurred.
- Every decision records who or what made it, so an operator reading a run afterwards can
  distinguish an action they chose, an action applied from advice on expiry, and a gate still
  waiting — without reconstructing it from timestamps.
- Applying advice on expiry is opt-in and does not change what the gate does while an operator is
  present: a selection that arrives before expiry governs, whatever the advisor recommended.
- The existing policies keep their current meanings, so a project that has not opted in sees no
  change in behaviour.

handoff.summary: Added an opt-in retry.escalate_timeout_policy ('preserve' default | 'apply_advice') that lets an expired escalate gate apply the advisory recommendation it just generated, via a timeout-only branch in _run_escalate_gate_inner that converts a usable recommendation into a taxonomy action before disposition normalization — so accept/defer/named behave exactly like deliberate selections. A new _advice_for_expired_gate helper withholds application for elevate, unparseable reports, empty recommendations, advisor launch failures, surfaces with no advisory, and recommendations this run cannot perform; each preserves the story with its own explanatory sentence in the result message. A new pending_hitl.cleanup_escalate_pending helper clears the expired checkpoint only when advice is actually applied. Two provenance fields (escalate_decision_source, escalate_timeout_advice) are populated for all seven gate outcomes and flow into the audit escalation block (with awaiting_operator and advisory_recommendation) and the resume record save/restore. The stale 'auto-escalating' timeout wording in pending.poll_pending and remote_gates was corrected without breaking the RCA pattern that matches it.

handoff.summary: Iteration 2 advisory cleanup, one P2. When an opted-in expiry applied an `accept` recommendation, the completion message still read 'Human approved via escalate gate' while the same run recorded escalate_decision_source=advisor_on_timeout — the account of the outcome contradicted the record of who produced it. Added _decided_by_advice(state), which reads that same published provenance field so message and record cannot disagree, and branched the approve-path completion message on it. Sweeping the file for the same pattern found it once more in the `named` disposition, whose log line said 'selected' and whose message said 'Worktree preserved for the operator' with no indication that no operator acted; both now name the expiry when the source is advisor_on_timeout. Operator-present wording is byte-identical in both branches. The other human-attribution strings in review_phase.py (984/989 human-review gate, 454 auto_approve policy) are unreachable from the advisor path and were left alone. _drive_gate now optionally captures _finalize_approve's kwargs, and four new tests pin both directions for both branches.

ac_verification.criterion: A recommendation of `elevate` on expiry leaves the story awaiting a human, because the taxonomy already treats it as the answer for a case no automated choice fits.

When no recommendation is available to apply — the advisor failed to launch, produced no parseable report, or recommended nothing — the gate preserves the story rather than selecting a fallback action. An absent recommendation is the absence of advice, not consent to any outcome, and the run states which of those two situations occurred.

Lines 228-249 define _TIMEOUT_ADVICE_NOTES with explanatory sentences for each, appended to preserve message at line 641. test_coord_escalate_timeout_advice.py::TestPreservesWhenAdviceCannotBeApplied covers all five with distinct message verification. Commit a3bc4b3c does not affect this logic.

- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 inspects 'the AdvisoryReport object that was just generated', but advisory is only bound inside the _is_pending_file_mode branch (review_phase.py:338). Referencing it at the post-normalization point (L367+) on a remote/interactive/no-interaction path would raise NameError.
  Suggestion: Initialize advisory: AdvisoryReport | None = None before the interaction-method dispatch at review_phase.py:334 and guard the new branch on advisory is not None.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3's 'clean up the expired pending checkpoint when advice is applied' has no named seam. _pending_escalate_gate has already rewritten the pending file with timed_out_awaiting_decision (pending_hitl.py:268-282) and returned before review_phase decides to apply advice; the cleanup helper (_pending.cleanup_pending) needs run_id and project_root, which review_phase resolves differently from pending_hitl.
  Suggestion: Either expose a small cleanup helper in pending_hitl.py that resolves the effective run_id/project_root the same way _pending_escalate_gate does, or pass the opt-in policy down so the timeout branch skips the preserve-rewrite when advice will be applied.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 adds validation with a clear ValueError for the new field, but load.py:1227 reads the existing escalate_policy with no validation at all, so the two fields will behave inconsistently on typos.
  Suggestion: Validate only the new field (as planned) and leave escalate_policy alone, or note the asymmetry; do not silently change escalate_policy's tolerance for unknown values, which would violate the last AC.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 mentions updating 'auto-escalating' timeout log wording, but pending_hitl.py:283-286 already says 'pending checkpoint preserved'. The stale wording lives on another surface (the dev/seam timeout or remote path).
  Suggestion: Grep for the literal 'auto-escalating' before editing so the fix lands on the surface that actually emits the message quoted in the spec, rather than rewording the already-correct escalate-gate log.
- [P2] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] In defaults.py, the newly documented configuration fields (escalate_policy, escalate_timeout_policy) should match the existing standard indentation and format of the retry section.
- [P2] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] Some test fixtures in test_sprint_rca.py write dummy logs that assert or contain the exact string 'Pending decision timed out after 10m 0s — auto-escalating'.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Step 2 changes the serialized escalation audit shape in src/theforge/coordinator/audit.py, but the plan does not call out the corresponding audit schema-version work. This repo has a writer-side schema guard in tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py, and additive audit fields normally require updating src/theforge/coordinator/audit_substrate.py schema metadata/migrations as well.
  Suggestion: When implementing Step 2, include the required CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION/migration updates and refresh the audit schema guard fixture alongside the new escalation provenance fields.

finding_registry.description: When an opted-in expired gate applies an accept recommendation, the successful outcome message still says the story was human-approved even though the recorded decision source is advisor_on_timeout.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
